children: Alcoa proposed a $2.6 billion debt offering to help fund the consideration for its proposed acquisition of some of South32 Limited's bauxite, alumina and aluminum smelter operations.

The alumina and aluminum products company said Wednesday the offering would consist of senior notes due in 2034 issued by Alumina and senior notes due in 2036 issued by Alcoa Nederland Holding. Both issuers are wholly-owned subsidiaries of Alcoa.
The company said it plans to use the proceeds from the offering, in addition to cash on hand, to fund the $3.1 billion cash portion of the consideration for the South32 deal.
Alcoa in June agreed to buy South32's bauxite, alumina and aluminum operations across Australia, Brazil and South Africa. The cash-and-stock deal is valued at up to $5.6 billion.
Alcoa said the notes will be sold in a private placement to people believed to be qualified institutional buyers.
